summary: Native read-only review of frozen digest 2c189ad0a6c54769e0f5c3904757a4a14a46add1a1e021e9327a9ff3ab733511. The named task, project, tag and tree shortcuts match the inspected API routes, and the corrected installer scope is mostly coherent. Published dependencies now invalidate the frozen Identity persistence, browser-return, feature-flag inventory and ADR assumptions. Two generic-operation contracts and the macOS acceptance floor also need clarification before implementation.

findings.description: The frozen device-authorization design places grants in JSON and coordinates grant consumption with file-backed session mutation through a new flock. The published modern-auth dependency makes auth.sqlite3 the sole transactional Identity authority and explicitly rejects sidecar proof storage when proof consumption and session issuance must commit together. Its sessions also carry auth_version, auth_method and provider-binding authority absent from the frozen model. Implementing the frozen plan would violate the accepted Identity contract and would not provide atomic grant consumption, session issuance, revocation and purge.
evidence: specs/023-agent-cli/plan.md:17 and :44 describe JSON grants and changes around the old SessionRepository; lines 58-63 require a new file authorization guard.
specs/023-agent-cli/data-model.md:9-22 defines data/device_authorizations/*.json as the authoritative device-grant store.
specs/023-agent-cli/contracts/device-auth.md:43-59 specifies consume-before-mint across atomic JSON and session files.

origin/feat/modern-auth at bc7fc72c35b7bf794eff912c07bdd38a1d1f0816, docs/decisions/0028-modern-identity-authority.md:10-18 requires one auth.sqlite3 authority and rejects a sidecar Identity store for consumed proofs and session issuance.
origin/feat/modern-auth:backend/app/repositories/auth_store.py defines users, sessions, attempts, challenges and proofs under one reusable BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction.
origin/feat/modern-auth:backend/app/repositories/session.py:54-123 stores and revokes sessions transactionally with auth_version, auth_method and provider_binding_id.
findings.recommendation: Rebase the CLI plan on the published modern-auth authority. Model device grants in auth.sqlite3 and consume the grant, recheck the approving session/account/version, and issue the CLI session within the shared AuthStore transaction. Update the data model, endpoint contract, purge/export behavior, failure semantics and tests to use the modern session fields and transaction lifecycle.

findings.description: The approved CLI journey requires /cli/authorize#user_code=... to survive sign-in, but the published shared login rejects that destination and drops fragments. A signed-out user following verification_uri_complete would return to the workspace root without the device code, so the browser/provider path in SC-006 cannot complete as frozen.

specs/023-agent-cli/plan.md:64 requires safe pathname/search/hash preservation through shared login.
specs/023-agent-cli/design.md:77-85 requires signed-out return to approval and manual-code recovery.

findings.recommendation: Reconcile the concrete modern-auth seam in the reviewed artifacts: allow the CLI approval route, preserve the code safely across email and external-provider redirects without putting it in query/access logs, and define manual re-entry when retained state is unavailable. Add acceptance for signed-out Google, Apple and email entry, callback return, refresh and expired state.

findings.description: The frozen rollout assumes five required managed rows plus optional cli_auth and treats unknown rows as degraded. Current origin/main has six required rows after task_mcp landed. A literal implementation of the reviewed contract would reject the current store or test the wrong upgrade and rollback topology.
evidence: specs/023-agent-cli/contracts/rollout.md:5 requires five existing rows plus optional cli_auth.
specs/023-agent-cli/plan.md:60-63 and tasks.md:39 require five-row absence and rollback evidence.
specs/023-agent-cli/contracts/device-auth.md:7 repeats the five-baseline-row assumption and strict unknown-row behavior.

origin/main at 21f08d26698a434f7b1d16b991b2b43d4e0ea0f2, backend/app/repositories/feature_flag.py:83-105 defines six managed flags, including task_mcp, and upgrades older healthy stores to that inventory.
origin/main:backend/app/core/config.py includes task_mcp in KNOWN_FEATURE_FLAGS and the runtime-managed set.
findings.recommendation: Update the reviewed baseline to six required rows and make cli_auth the optional seventh entry. Rework seed, upgrade, read, mutate, scrub, rollback and malformed/unknown-row cases against the merged task_mcp inventory, then refresh the ADR binding and frozen artifact digest.

findings.description: The mandatory CLI planning gate requires acceptance of a proposed ADR-0028, but the published modern-auth dependency already owns accepted ADR-0028 for the Identity authority that this feature must extend. Both records cannot remain authoritative under the same number, and the rollout contract is hash-bound to the obsolete identifier.
evidence: specs/023-agent-cli/plan.md:38 requires acceptance of docs/decisions/0028-runtime-managed-cli-authentication.md.
specs/023-agent-cli/tasks.md:6 and :64 make that ADR acceptance an implementation prerequisite.
specs/023-agent-cli/contracts/rollout.md:3 and :15 identify ADR-0028 and bind its current SHA-256.
origin/feat/modern-auth:docs/decisions/0028-modern-identity-authority.md:1-6 is already marked accepted and supersedes the JSON-backed Identity assumptions relevant to CLI authorization.
findings.recommendation: Reserve a new decision number for CLI authorization after reconciling current refs. Make accepted modern-identity ADR-0028 an explicit dependency, rewrite the CLI decision around its transactional authority, and update every reference and reviewed digest binding.

findings.description: FR-002 authorizes generic deployed member JSON operations, while the CLI contract syntactically permits any path below the API prefix and reserves only /auth/device/*. The current and published APIs also contain public authentication, operator/admin and specialized authentication routes. The contract therefore does not enforce its stated member-operation boundary and permits generic logout to revoke a session without the source-aware local cleanup promised by auth logout.
evidence: specs/023-agent-cli/spec.md:47 and :94 limit the promise to deployed member JSON operations while preserving authorization rules.
specs/023-agent-cli/contracts/cli.md:26 and :29 accept arbitrary generic API methods/paths below api_prefix and reserve only device-auth paths.
backend/app/api/auth.py:85-168 exposes signup, login, logout and me under the same prefix.
backend/app/api/admin.py:94-307 exposes operator-only account and feature-flag mutations under the same prefix.
origin/feat/modern-auth:specs/022-modern-auth/contracts/http-auth.md adds many proof, provider and sensitive account operations under /api/auth and /api/account.
findings.recommendation: Define an enforceable generic-operation inventory consistent with FR-002. Explicitly exclude public, operator and specialized auth operations from generic dispatch, and state which sensitive authenticated account operations remain member operations. Test that generic dispatch cannot bypass source-aware auth logout or specialized credential handling.

findings.description: The contract allows field selection for generic responses and requires unknown selectors to fail, but arbitrary generic response fields cannot be known locally without an extra schema request. For a POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE, discovering an unknown field after a confirmed 2xx response would report failure after the mutation was applied, without the delivery_unknown semantics reserved for transport uncertainty.
evidence: specs/023-agent-cli/contracts/cli.md:29 permits generic POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE.
specs/023-agent-cli/contracts/cli.md:35 requires malformed or unknown selectors to fail.
specs/023-agent-cli/contracts/cli.md:29 and :35 allow --fields on generic bodies while only named schemas are locally known.
specs/023-agent-cli/plan.md:23 and :54-56 require one business request and no implicit schema lookup or automatic replay.
specs/023-agent-cli/contracts/cli.md:60 marks writes uncertain only when interrupted after dispatch.
findings.recommendation: Choose a safe deterministic rule before implementation: either disallow response-field selection on generic mutations unless it can be validated before dispatch, or make post-response projection problems return confirmed mutation success with explicit projection metadata. Add a fixture proving callers are never encouraged to repeat an already-applied mutation.

findings.description: The feature promises native macOS x86_64 and arm64 releases and claims explicit platform limits, but the minimum supported macOS version is deferred until publication. SC-004 proves native jobs, while SC-005's Unix/Windows wording can be satisfied without a released-install run at a declared macOS floor. The supported-machine acceptance scenario is therefore not currently measurable for either Mac target.
evidence: specs/023-agent-cli/spec.md:60-62 accepts installation on a supported machine, and FR-009 at :101 includes both macOS architectures.
specs/023-agent-cli/plan.md:19 leaves the macOS minimum to future build/link evidence.
specs/023-agent-cli/contracts/distribution.md:11-12 leaves both Mac runtime floors undocumented until before publish.
specs/023-agent-cli/spec.md:119-121 requires native build smoke but describes actual released installation only as Unix/Windows.
specs/023-agent-cli/checklists/requirements.md:18 claims supported platforms are already explicit.
findings.recommendation: Before implementation freeze, record a numeric minimum macOS version selected from native link/run evidence and add released-asset installation smoke at that floor for both Mac architectures, or explicitly narrow the published acceptance matrix. This is an implementing-agent platform decision under the owner-approved scope.
